Always-on VPN without blocking · Set up
As Android says now, while ProxyFlow is connected.
As Android said at %1$s, while ProxyFlow was connected.
Android tells ProxyFlow only while it\'s connected.
With the system kill switch on, apps have no internet while ProxyFlow is off. Turn it off in Android\'s VPN settings to use your normal network.
ProxyFlow already blocks traffic while it\'s running. If Android stops ProxyFlow, or another VPN takes over, only Android itself can keep blocking.
Tap the settings icon next to ProxyFlow.
Turn on Block connections without VPN.
Menu names vary by phone maker. With blocking on, apps can\'t go online while ProxyFlow is off — turn it off again in the same place to use your normal network.
ProxyFlow can\'t turn this on for you: only you can, in Android\'s settings. Android tells ProxyFlow whether it\'s on only while ProxyFlow is connected.
If Android stops ProxyFlow — to free memory, say — it may not start it again: with blocking on, apps then stay offline until you open ProxyFlow and connect.
Android lets some of its own services reach the network outside any VPN, also with blocking on.
